title: Confidential Information and Unauthorized Disclosure
definition: A secrecy violation occurs when a person discloses, shares, forwards, provides access to, requests, obtains, or improperly handles confidential, restricted, proprietary, sensitive, or otherwise protected company information without appropriate authorization. The model must evaluate the meaning and context of the communication and must not rely only on confidentiality-related keywords.
violations: Disclosing confidential or restricted company information to an unauthorized person
Sharing confidential documents, files, customer information, business information, financial information, technical information, or internal company information with an unauthorized recipient
Forwarding or providing access to protected company information without authorization
Improperly handling confidential information in a way that exposes it to unauthorized individuals
Requesting or encouraging another person to disclose protected company information without authorization
Requesting another person to provide confidential information that they are not authorized to share
Sending protected information to a personal account or unauthorized external recipient
Sharing confidential information through an unauthorized communication channel
Providing restricted information to someone who does not have a legitimate business need to receive it
Attempting to bypass confidentiality controls to obtain or share protected information
Attempting to conceal an unauthorized disclosure of protected information
Using protected company information for an unauthorized personal or external purpose
exceptions: Legitimate instructions to keep information confidential
Instructions that prevent disclosure until an agreement, contract, or authorization is completed
Disclosure explicitly authorized by the appropriate company authority
Sharing information with an explicitly authorized recipient
Routine business communication that does not disclose protected information
Mentioning confidentiality, agreements, contracts, projects, customers, or documents without disclosing protected information
Discussing the importance of protecting confidential information
Requesting authorization before sharing protected information
Reporting a suspected unauthorized disclosure to an appropriate authority
examples: Sending a confidential company document to an unauthorized external recipient
Forwarding restricted business information to an unauthorized person
Providing an unauthorized person access to confidential company files
Sending customer information to a personal email account without authorization
Asking a colleague to send confidential project information to an external contact
Telling someone not to disclose an agreement until it is formally signed is not a violation
Discussing confidentiality without revealing protected information is not a violation
Mentioning a confidential project without revealing confidential information is not automatically a violation

title: Improper Payments, Gifts, and Benefits
definition: A market bribery violation occurs when a person offers, promises, gives, requests, accepts, or arranges an improper payment, gift, benefit, favor, service, hospitality, entertainment, or other advantage with the purpose or expectation of improperly influencing a business, commercial, regulatory, or market-related decision. The model must understand the relationship between the benefit and the intended decision rather than flagging individual words such as gift, drinks, dinner, payment, or entertainment.
violations: Offering money or another improper benefit in exchange for favorable business treatment
Requesting or accepting an improper payment or benefit to influence a business decision
Offering a gift with the intention of improperly influencing a decision
Offering meals, drinks, entertainment, travel, services, favors, or hospitality to improperly influence a decision
Agreeing to provide an improper benefit in return for preferential treatment
Using an intermediary or third party to provide an improper payment or benefit intended to influence a business decision
Discussing or arranging an improper payment or benefit to obtain an unfair business advantage
Requesting a personal payment, gift, favor, service, or benefit in exchange for approving or influencing a business activity
Offering benefits to a decision-maker before a business decision with the intention of obtaining favorable treatment
Arranging entertainment, drinks, meals, gifts, or other benefits specifically to influence a business, commercial, regulatory, or market decision
Attempting to conceal or disguise an improper payment or benefit
Encouraging another person to provide an improper benefit to obtain preferential treatment
exceptions: Legitimate business expenses permitted under company policy
Ordinary business activities without an attempt to improperly influence a decision
Benefits explicitly permitted and authorized under company policy
Routine discussion of gifts, meals, drinks, entertainment, expenses, or business benefits without an improper purpose
Approved business hospitality without improper influence
Legitimate company events and social activities
Rejecting, reporting, or discussing concerns about a potentially improper payment or benefit
Ordinary personal or social discussion that has no connection to influencing a business decision
examples: Offering money to a business partner in exchange for awarding a contract
Offering an expensive gift to influence a customer's purchasing decision
Requesting a personal payment in exchange for approving a transaction
Arranging for another person to provide a benefit in exchange for preferential treatment
Offering drinks or entertainment specifically to obtain favorable business treatment
Offering a gift immediately before a business decision with the intention of influencing the decision
Discussing an ordinary business dinner without improper influence is not bribery
Mentioning gifts or drinks without an improper business purpose is not automatically bribery

title: Artificial or Misleading Market Activity
definition: A market manipulation violation occurs when a person intentionally attempts to artificially influence the price, supply, demand, trading activity, or market perception of a financial instrument through deceptive, misleading, coordinated, or artificial actions. The model must understand the intended market behavior rather than relying on words such as buy, sell, price, volume, market, or trading.
violations: Intentionally creating artificial buying or selling activity to influence a market price
Coordinating transactions to artificially increase or decrease a financial instrument's price
Creating false or misleading market activity to influence other market participants
Spreading false or misleading information with the intention of influencing trading activity or market prices
Using deceptive transactions or trading strategies to create a false impression of market demand or supply
Encouraging another person to participate in activity intended to artificially influence market conditions
Planning transactions specifically to create an artificial market price
Coordinating with others to create artificial demand, supply, volume, or trading activity
Instructing another person to create misleading market activity
Intentionally distributing false information to influence trading decisions
Attempting to conceal an artificial or deceptive trading strategy
Creating a false appearance of market interest, liquidity, demand, supply, or trading volume
exceptions: Legitimate market analysis
Ordinary trading or investment decisions for legitimate business or investment purposes
Accurate communication of publicly available market information
Legitimate discussion of market conditions without instructions to manipulate activity
General discussion of prices, markets, securities, trading, or investment strategies
Legitimate research or analysis without an intention to manipulate
Good-faith discussion of possible market scenarios
Reporting suspected market manipulation for legitimate compliance purposes
examples: Coordinating transactions specifically to artificially increase a security's price
Creating misleading trading activity to make demand appear higher than it is
Sharing intentionally false information to influence another person's trading decision
Planning transactions specifically to create an artificial market price
Asking others to create buying activity so a security appears more popular
Coordinating trades to make trading volume appear artificially high
Discussing normal market conditions without manipulation is not a violation
Legitimate market analysis is not market manipulation

title: Employee Ethical Conduct
definition: An employee ethics violation occurs when an employee engages in dishonest, deceptive, inappropriate, unprofessional, improper, or unethical conduct that conflicts with company standards, employee responsibilities, or expected professional behavior. Employee ethics includes inappropriate workplace behavior, improper employee relationships, inappropriate social activities connected to work, misuse of position or company resources, conflicts of interest, and attempts to conceal improper conduct. The model must understand the overall meaning and context rather than relying on individual keywords.
violations: Knowingly providing false or misleading information for an improper purpose
Using an employee's position, authority, access, or influence for an improper personal benefit
Engaging in dishonest or deceptive conduct related to company business
Intentionally concealing relevant information to obtain an improper benefit
Using company resources, information, systems, or authority for an unauthorized personal purpose
Engaging in an undisclosed or improperly managed conflict of interest
Using an employee's position or company relationship to obtain improper preferential treatment
Engaging in inappropriate, unprofessional, disrespectful, or improper behavior in a work-related context
Making inappropriate requests, suggestions, arrangements, or instructions involving employees or business contacts
Encouraging or arranging inappropriate conduct involving employees
Engaging in inappropriate social, personal, drinking, alcohol, entertainment, or similar activities connected to workplace conduct
Using workplace relationships to facilitate inappropriate personal behavior
Attempting to conceal inappropriate employee behavior from management, HR, compliance, or the company
Requesting another employee to participate in improper or unethical conduct
Knowingly violating expected professional standards for a personal or improper advantage
exceptions: Ordinary mistakes without intentional dishonesty or improper conduct
Good-faith business decisions
Legitimate use of company resources for authorized business purposes
Routine professional communication
Casual, informal, incomplete, or unclear communication without sufficient evidence of improper conduct
Clearly personal communication unrelated to workplace responsibilities or employee conduct
Legitimate employee social activities
Authorized company-sponsored social events
Ordinary discussion of food, drinks, restaurants, entertainment, meetings, or social activities without evidence of inappropriate conduct
Good-faith reporting of inappropriate behavior
Legitimate requests for clarification or assistance
examples: Knowingly providing false information to obtain an improper personal benefit
Using an employee's position to obtain preferential treatment
Concealing a conflict of interest
Using company information for an unauthorized personal purpose
Using company resources for an unauthorized personal activity
Making an inappropriate request to another employee
Arranging inappropriate conduct involving employees
Engaging in inappropriate behavior during a company-related event
Arranging inappropriate drinking or alcohol-related activity involving employees in a work-related context
Encouraging employees to participate in inappropriate social or drinking activity connected to work
Attempting to hide improper employee behavior
A normal social discussion about drinks without inappropriate context is not automatically an ethics violation

title: Complaint Handling and Reporting
definition: A complaints-related violation occurs when a legitimate complaint or concern involving employee conduct, business practices, or company processes is improperly ignored, suppressed, mishandled, discouraged, concealed, or intentionally prevented from reaching the appropriate reporting or review process. The model must distinguish between reporting or discussing a complaint and attempting to suppress or improperly handle it.
violations: Intentionally preventing a legitimate complaint from being reported
Ignoring a complaint requiring investigation or appropriate handling
Suppressing or concealing a legitimate complaint or concern
Improperly handling a formal complaint to prevent appropriate review
Discouraging a person from reporting a legitimate concern
Retaliating against or improperly treating a person because they raised a legitimate complaint
Telling someone not to report a legitimate workplace concern
Attempting to hide a complaint from compliance, HR, management, or another appropriate authority
Destroying, withholding, or manipulating information to prevent investigation of a legitimate complaint
Attempting to close or resolve a legitimate complaint outside the required process specifically to prevent review
Threatening or pressuring a person to withdraw a legitimate complaint
Instructing another person to conceal or suppress a legitimate complaint
exceptions: Simply reporting a legitimate concern or complaint
Routine communication about a complaint
Resolving a complaint through an authorized company process
Requesting additional information needed to investigate a complaint
Discussing the existence or status of a complaint without suppressing it
Providing legitimate assistance to someone reporting a concern
Forwarding a complaint to the appropriate team
Requesting clarification about a complaint in good faith
Discussing a complaint without attempting to influence whether it is reported or investigated
examples: Telling an employee not to report a workplace concern
Ignoring a formal complaint requiring investigation
Preventing a complaint from reaching compliance
Suppressing a complaint to avoid investigation
Threatening an employee because they submitted a complaint
Asking someone to withdraw a complaint to avoid investigation
Reporting a legitimate complaint is not a violation
Requesting information needed to investigate a complaint is not a violation

title: Unauthorized Communication Channels
definition: A change in communication violation occurs when business-related communication is moved, continued, redirected, or intentionally arranged through a personal or external communication channel that is not approved for company business. The model must determine whether the communication is actually business-related and whether the external channel is unauthorized. It must not flag an email merely because it mentions WhatsApp, personal email, phone, social media, drinks, meetings, or another communication method.
violations: Moving a business discussion from an approved company channel to a personal or external communication channel
Asking another person to continue business-related communication through a personal or external messaging service
Using a personal or external communication service to continue discussions concerning company business, agreements, transactions, or work-related matters
Redirecting business communication to an external channel to avoid or bypass an approved company communication system
Continuing a business discussion through an external communication method when the communication concerns company work or a business agreement
Requesting a colleague or business contact to use a personal account for company-related communication
Moving confidential, transactional, contractual, or work-related discussions to an unauthorized external channel
Using a personal phone, email, messaging application, or other external service to conduct company business when the channel is not approved
Attempting to avoid company monitoring, retention, approval, or compliance controls by moving business communication externally
Arranging future business communication through an unauthorized external channel
exceptions: The external communication channel is explicitly approved for the relevant business activity
The communication is clearly personal and unrelated to company business
The external channel is used for a legitimate purpose specifically authorized by the company
Mentioning WhatsApp, personal email, phone, or another external service without requesting business communication through it
Personal communication unrelated to company business
Discussing an external communication channel without moving or requesting movement of business communication
Using an approved external communication service for an authorized business purpose
Discussing personal social activities without moving business communication to an unauthorized channel
examples: Asking a business contact to continue a company discussion through a personal messaging service
Moving a business agreement discussion to an external messaging application
Asking someone to continue company communication through a personal account
Inviting a business contact to continue work-related communication outside the approved company system
Asking a colleague to send company documents to a personal email address
Moving a business transaction discussion to a personal messaging application to avoid monitoring
Mentioning WhatsApp in an unrelated personal conversation is not a violation
Discussing plans to meet socially without moving business communication externally is not a violation
